concept.title: Figures and diagrams
concept.shortdesc: Figures carry GOV.UK-styled captions, and the DITA SVG domain embeds scalable diagrams that stay crisp at any size.

The same diagram referenced directly by path:

Local SVG diagrams are inlined as native SVG, so any links inside a diagram are clickable and the artwork stays crisp at any size. Each image also receives an accessible name derived from the figure title, the caption is numbered automatically, and the diagram never overflows the content column. Set govuk.svg.inline=no to keep the plain image rendering instead.

section.title: How an inlined diagram is named
section.p: A diagram with a title is named by it, and a desc describes it. An author may point at them explicitly with aria-labelledby and aria-describedby on the root svg. Inlining gives every id in the file a prefix that is unique to that instance, so several diagrams can share a page; the plugin gives the same prefix to every token in aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-owns, aria-controls, aria-flowto, aria-activedescendant, aria-details and aria-errormessage, so each still names the element the author meant. A diagram with no title takes an aria-label from the figure title.

The role depends on what the diagram holds. A diagram without links is a picture: it gets role="img", and its title and desc serve as its name and description. A diagram with links is not, because an image has no children a reader can reach and axe-core reports links nested in one. It gets role="group" instead, named by its title through aria-labelledby and described by its desc through aria-describedby; the plugin gives either one an id when the file has none. An aria-labelledby or aria-label the author wrote is left as written. Give a linked diagram a title, and list its links in the text as well, so that readers who do not use the diagram reach the same pages.

section.title: Diagrams and the content policy
section.p: An inlined diagram becomes part of the page, so it is treated as code, not as an image. By default the build removes anything in an SVG file that would run or fetch in the reader's browser — script, foreignObject, event-handler attributes, links whose scheme runs code, and images or fragments fetched from another origin — and reports what it found and removed (GOVK004W). Ordinary links to other websites inside a diagram are kept. A publisher who wants the file exactly as authored sets govuk.svg.sanitize=no; the report still appears. Diagrams are inlined only from under the input directory (govuk.inline.scope); a reference that points elsewhere on the build machine is reported and rendered as an image instead. Attributes that arrive only as SVG 1.1 doctype defaults (contentScriptType, zoomAndPan and their kin) are dropped, so tool-generated diagrams validate.

The same policy covers images and objects fetched from another origin and links whose scheme runs code anywhere in a topic: each is reported (GOVK006W), rendered as authored under govuk.content.policy=warn, or replaced by a marked placeholder under strip. Nothing here ever fails a build. The guidance for authors and the hosting headers that complete the picture are in ; every code is listed in .
